overview.description: Bouillotte is a historic 18th-century French gambling game that represents a critical evolution in the history of Poker. Emerging during the French Revolution as a derivative of Brelan, it is a fast-paced vying game for 3-5 players. It is unique for its use of a stripped pack and a 'retourné' (turned card) that can complete a player's Brelan into a Brelan Carré (four-of-a-kind). It famously introduced the concept of the 'Cave' (fixed chip stack), which restricted betting to the chips currently on the table.

history.origins: Bouillotte was developed in late 18th-century France as a modification of Brelan to regulate betting behavior during the volatile Revolutionary period. It became so popular that it influenced the development of early American Stud Poker.
timeline: 1789: Bouillotte gains popularity in Parisian gambling dens.
1830s: Featured prominently in the literature of Balzac and Thackeray.
1870s: Replaced by modern Poker in international gambling circles.
Present: A rare historical game studied for its influence on the betting structures of modern gambling.
history.evolution: The game moved from the simple 3-card vying of Brelan to a format where a community card (the retourné) added a dramatic fifth card to the potential combinations.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'Enlightenment Game', its rules on the 'Cave' were a precursor to modern 'Table Stakes' in casino poker.

setup.players: 4 players are standard (using 20 cards). 3 players remove Queens (16 cards). 5 players add Jacks (24 cards).
setup.deck: A stripped piquet pack: Ace, King, Queen, 9, 8 in each suit. Ranking: A-K-Q-9-8.
setup.dealing: Players ante into the pot. Dealer deals 3 cards to each player and turns the next card face-up (the retourné).

rules.objective: Win the pot by holding the highest hand or by forcing all other players to fold during the vying rounds.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: Each player puts a fixed amount in the pot. 2. **Deal**: Players receive 3 cards and see the retourné. 3. **Vying**: Starting left of dealer, players bet, call, or fold. 4. **Showdown**: Best hand wins. Hand hierarchy: Brelan Carré (four of a kind using retourné), Brelan Favori (three of a kind including retourné), simple Brelan (three of a kind), then highest point-total in a suit.
keyRules: The 'Cave' rule: You cannot bet more than the chips you have on the table.
If no Brelan is held, the player with the highest total value in a single suit wins.
Aces are worth 11, face cards 10, others face value.

strategy.basic: Only bet aggressively if you hold a pair that matches the retourné, as this guaranteed a Brelan Favori.
strategy.intermediate: Pot Odds: Calculate the total chips in the pot versus your remaining Cave. If you are 'Pot Committed', folding becomes mathematically incorrect.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing on Suit Totals: Since a Brelan is rare, most pots are won on suit totals. If the retourné is an Ace, bluffing that you have high cards in that suit is a standard tactic.
tips: Manage your Cave carefully; losing it all means you must buy back in or exit.
Pay close attention to the retourné—it is the most important card on the table.

list.name: Brelan (Parent Game)
list.description: The older version without the retourné card; play is purely based on the 3-card hand.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Listed to document Bouillotte's parent game; no separate engine overrides are modeled for Brelan.

difficulty.easy: Bets blindly on any pair. Never bluffs. Folds to any raise.
difficulty.medium: Follows basic vying heuristics. Understands the value of the Brelan Favori. Folds on low suit totals.
difficulty.hard: Expert bluffing model. Calculates exact equity of Brelan vs Suit Total. Tracks opponent betting patterns to detect bluffs.

considerations: Requires a vying engine capable of handling 'Table Stakes' (Cave) logic.
Hand evaluation must prioritize Brelans before calculating suit totals.

additional: The History of Gambling in France (Sorbonne Press)

ante.description: Contribute a fixed amount to the central pot.
ante.constraints: Allowed only during the ante phase.

deal.reason: The initial distribution of three cards and the turning of the retourné are handled by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: The only public card is the retourné turned from the stock; no separate market area exists in the game.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from a market; hand strength is determined solely by the deal and retourné.

buy_stock.reason: There is no drawing or buying from the stock during play; the cards are distributed in a fixed deal.

fold.description: Abandon the hand and forfeit all contributions to the pot.
fold.constraints: Allowed during the vying phase when facing a bet or raise.

check.description: Pass the action without wagering when no bet is active.
check.constraints: Only available when no previous bet has been made in the round.

call.description: Match the current wager to remain in the round.
call.constraints: Allowed only during the vying phase when a bet is active.

bet.description: Place a wager into the pot.
bet.constraints: Must be within the limits of the player's Cave (chips on table).

raise.constraints: Must not exceed the player's available Cave.

declare.reason: Hand resolution is based on public card reveal at showdown rather than a formal declaration phase.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until the system triggers the showdown reveal logic at the end of vying.

award_pot.description: Divide the pot among the winner(s) at showdown.

play_card.reason: Bouillotte is a vying/betting game where cards are held for comparison rather than played to tricks.

draw.reason: The entire hand is distributed at the start; no drawing phase exists during the play of the hand.

discard.reason: Players must keep all cards dealt to them; cards are only removed to the muck after the round ends.

pass.reason: Players must check, bet, or fold during their turn; a simple pass without action is not supported.

bid.reason: Bouillotte uses a wagering system rather than an auction-style bidding system for contracts.

meld.reason: Hand resolution is based on five-card combinations rather than forming and laying melds on the table.

go_out.reason: The round concludes automatically after the final showdown and pot distribution are completed.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: The three-card hand is fixed after the deal; no draw pile exists during the wagering rounds.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: All cards are retained until the showdown; no separate discard or recycling pile is used.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and point values to combinations; no card has a secondary action effect.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Wagering is performed via direct placement of chips; no hidden declaration tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Bouillotte is a vying/betting game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: This game is not a shedding game; players maintain their hands throughout the deal.
notApplicableReasons.bankingConfig: There is no separate banker; all betting flows directly into a common pot funded by player caves.

customLogicNeeded: Suit point-total calculation for non-brelan hands.

customActions.description: Distribute three cards to each player and turn one card face-up as the retourné.
Determine hand hierarchy including Brelans and Suit Totals.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; specialized Brelan hierarchy determines the winning hand at showdown.
engine.deckDescription: One stripped 20-card pack: five ranks (ace, king, queen, nine, eight) in each of four French suits. No jokers; used for Bouillotte (French gambling game) where four players receive five cards and the best point total or sequence wins the pot.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Each suit has five cards; suits are used for building sequences (brelan, flux) and for comparing hands. The point total (aces 11, kings and queens 10, nines and eights face value) may determine the winner.
engine.rankDescription: Five ranks per suit: ace (11 points), king (10), queen (10), nine (9), eight (8). Point total determines the base hand value; sequences (three or four of a kind, or four of same suit) may outrank point totals in Bouillotte.
engine.dealPattern: Cards are dealt individually clockwise starting from left of dealer.

hero.title: BOUILLOTTE
hero.subtitle: The Revolutionary Gambler
hero.tagline: Strip the deck. Bet the Cave. Rule the Brelan.

synthesis.shortDescription: The precursor to American stud poker. A high-speed vying game from the French Revolution where a single turned card can turn a simple pair into a legendary Brelan Carré. Manage your Cave, read your rivals, and master the art of the Enlightenment bluff.

prompts.human: The pot is 100 fiches. The retourné is the Ace of Hearts. You hold the Ace of Spades and Ace of Clubs. You have a Brelan Favori! Raise the bet to 50 and make them pay to see the cards.
prompts.ai: Game: Bouillotte. Type: Vying. Rules: 3 cards + 1 community. Hierarchy: Brelan Carré > Brelan Favori > Brelan > Suit Total. Table stakes (Cave) enforced.

scoring.winCondition: Best hand at showdown or all opponents fold.

penalties.Bust Cave: Running out of chips in your Cave results in forced exit or rebuy.

scoring.splitRules: Ties are broken by the player closest to the dealer's right (following play direction).

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target; play until the session ends or one player has all chips.
